newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank group says Thailand has not sought aid.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank group says Thailand has not sought aid.

text.p: Japanese banks have not received any requests from the government of Thailand to support a financial rescue scheme for the country, said Naotaka Saeki, chairman of the Federation of Bankers Associations of Japan.

Saeki, also president of Sanwa Bank Ltd, told a regular news conference that Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya will visit the federation on Thursday to explain to Japanese bankers the recent situation regarding the Thai currency. Saeki did not give further details regarding the visit.

Banking industry sources have said that some Japanese banks are likely to participate in a rescue scheme for Thailand if they are asked to do so, as Japanese banks and companies have already made a substantial commitment to the Thai economy through direct investments.

Thailand said last week that it would try to raise a total of $10 billion, consisting of $5 billion in loans from banks and $5 billion in bond issues, in order to replenish reserves that were severely depleted when it defended its currency against speculative attacks in May.
